explanation: The annotation scheme is a representational choice that makes solution reconstruction possible. explanation: This is the mechanism the passage offers in place of Cook's full proof. Decision problems are recast as language-acceptance problems: F answers YES on input I exactly when a transformed string I' belongs to a language L. Turing machines are the model of computation that accepts such languages, and a universal Turing machine can take a description of any machine plus an input string and simulate it. Because the machine's configuration and transitions are finite and local, they can be written as a Boolean expression whose satisfying assignments correspond to accepting computations. The passage emphasizes the dual role of Turing machines: simple enough that the transformation to Boolean expressions can be constructed, yet rich enough to compute any function an ordinary computer can.
